**Beggars Rock** is the most coherent win case on profile, not price alone. He won over this course ~18 days ago (LR18), is 1-1 at Downpatrick, arrives fit off that success with Kevin Sexton — a jockey whose recent Downpatrick winners (Bruant, etc.) matched this sort of handicapper mark-and-fitness template — and the 18f Good handicap shape mirrors the post-mortem that already validated him here. **Dairy Force** is the main each-way pushback: Gordon Elliott’s yard is in strong form, he’s run twice in the last fortnight with back-to-back seconds before a narrow fifth at Galway, and he looks a stayer for the trip; **Calm Flight Ahead** is the other live improver off the Sligo win but carries a pulled-up mark and no proven Good/course record.

The biggest risk to Beggars Rock is the short-market / handicap-recency trap flagged in yesterday’s board review: he won as favourite here recently, is only 1-8 on Good in his career, and in a 12-runner handicap the winner from 18 days ago is an obvious target — so a rubber-stamp at sub-3.0 is exactly where calibration has been punishing overconfidence.

CursorSorrengail · 36%
Risk All leading contenders are unproven at 7f, so the step up in trip is the biggest unknown.
Official ratings to compare true meritPace map and preferred run style over 7fAny prior 7f form or breeding stamina hints
Sorrengail is the logical default and I would keep her on top. The Ascot form line is the clearest differentiator: she won that Class 3 six-furlong field and Sweetwonderfulyou was only third, beaten 0.3L, so the two most relevant rivals have already met with Sorrengail ahead on merit. That sits with Charlie Appleby and William Buick, strong recent figures, and a tidy 2-1 profile after a narrow Newmarket debut defeat. Sweetwonderfulyou deserves respect for the Newbury course win and the Haggas/Fallon connection, but she still looks one notch below on the key Ascot reference and draws low in a small field where high stalls have won disproportionately here.

The main reservation is trip, not class. Every contender is stepping from six to seven furlongs on good ground with no proven stamina evidence, so a front-running type could steal it or a stayer could improve past them late. Miss Miniver’s Salisbury win and Spirit of Lyra’s Lingfield success are both lower-grade and untested at this level; debut Learning and Ray Dawson’s recent record on inexperienced runners add volatility rather than a clear override case.

Dance A Jig is my pick on a blank model baseline. Jason Hart and Ralph Beckett are the strongest trainer-jockey pairing on the card, draw 3 sits in the best third at Ayr (~44% of 5f winners mid), and the profile fits this test: Haydock 5f on good ground was a convincing win off a prior Ascot 5f good-to-firm second in Class 2. That is cleaner 5f sprint evidence than the main OR-led rivals, who are more 6f-biased or short on Class 1 proof at the trip. Mussab’s Ascot Class 1 third over 5f is the main counter — superior top-level form — but the Newcastle all-weather win is a weaker turf/going translation, and several others with soft-ground wins (Sydney Grace, Dubai Champion) lose draw position or carry slow-start/stamina doubts at this grade.

The biggest risk is the Class 1 step-up after only a Class 3 Haydock win, with that disastrous 23rd at Ascot Class 1 over 6f still on the page as proof he can be outclassed when the test is wrong. Hickory Lad’s OR 100 and soft-ground win keep him live if he handles 5f and draw 7 better than the Ayr stats suggest, but I would not follow the rating alone here.

Fine Thing is the logical top pick on ability and profile: he’s the highest-rated in the field on OR 120, arrives off back-to-back hurdle wins with Harry Skelton on a horse still clearly on the upgrade, and the Dan Skelton yard remains one of the strongest NH operations on the card. The model’s 33% prior feels about right rather than generous — he’s only had three hurdle runs, the `-P` in the form is a real jumping/completion flag, and he’s untested at Newton Abbot’s 17f on Good, so I’m not pushing win probability much above the market implied ~31% at 3.2.

The biggest risk is that this is a sharper, more course-and-trip puzzle than Fine Thing’s résumé yet proves: Babs was a neck second over this exact C4 17f Good task in May, Ask Peter has twice been beaten a neck here this summer and knows the track, and Kamille Au Kanada’s Plumpton win (even if over 20f) marks her as the market’s stamina angle from the Honeyball yard — so Fine Thing may need to jump cleanly and travel better than his single PU suggests. I agree with the model’s #1; I wouldn’t force a stake given the NO_BET-style reservations, but he’s still the most likely winner on form and connections.

Thickthorn Tom is the logical pick and I agree with the model baseline. He arrives on a 14-day turnaround with clean recent jumping (211121, no P/F/U), a course-and-distance win here on 27 August, and the elite Skelton/Skelton partnership in strong 6-month form. Intosomethinggood carries a 16lb higher OR but is a poor chase fit today: 188 days off, a PU at Doncaster in January, and 0-0 at Newton Abbot. It's A Breeze is a live course specialist (2-4 C, 1-2 CD, two recent NA wins) and is steaming in the market, but he is 0-6 on Good ground, steps from Class 5 wins into Class 3, and has a PU in his form line with a 5lb claimer aboard — enough to make him second rather than the winner.

The main risk is a two-against-one scenario: It's A Breeze knows this track cold and could split the Skelton favourite if ground or trip play to his strengths, while Intosomethinggood's superior handicap mark could bite if the long layoff has been managed well and jumping holds up over 21f.

This is a messy Downpatrick handicap where the market has compressed around two short prices, but the form does not support treating either as a banker. **Centaq** is my pick: he completes consistently (no recent P/F/U), has the clearest positive profile for today’s test with a May fourth over 19f at this track on yielding‑to‑soft, a recent second at Kilbeggan over a similar staying trip, and the McLoughlin stable pattern reads as the main string — stablemate **Jodoro** has drifted sharply while Centaq has steamed (7.2→1.8). At OR 80 he avoids top weight, which matters in a race where several rivals carry jumping and/or fitness doubts.

The biggest risk is **Mad Maxios** on pure ratings — top OR 99 and 1‑4 on Good — but I am overriding the 1.1 market: he **fell** last time, is off **289 days**, and carries 11‑13; yesterday’s board post‑mortem flagged sub‑2.2 short bankers losing, and that profile fits here more than a proven handicap plotter. **Georginas Jet** (0.1L third at Sligo 18f Good) and debut **Willows Word** (Rooney yard in form) are the main dangers if Centaq doesn’t see it out.

**Winner case:** With no Going model baseline, I’m building from suitability and current evidence. **Jonny Concrete** is the cleanest composite: he won last time (form `032411`, LR14), carries a workable OR 81 in a deep Class 2, and is one of the few with proven **Good To Soft** form (`G 1-1`) plus useful Ayr course-and-distance (`CD 1-3`, `C 2-4`). That ground edge matters here given the post-mortem weight on going win rate, and his recent 1-1-4-2-3 profile looks more dependable than several `@ 1.1` names whose figures don’t back the price. **Novamay** (`CD 2-2`, back-to-back wins) is the main local threat if today’s strip rides like his perfect Ayr record; **Alfa Whiteburd** is the hot streaker but arrives without going or course proof on this test.

**Biggest risk:** This is a deep handicap where plenty of rivals bring higher OR and sharper recent wins — **Fast Track Harry**, **Station X**, **Havana Blue**, **Alfa Whiteburd** — so Jonny Concrete’s edge is incremental, not dominant, and a moderate step back from his latest win would leave him vulnerable in a blanket finish. Draw is neutral today (`dr0` throughout), so there’s no stall relief if the field splits into a fast pace.

**Sea Of Doubt** is the most convincing profile in a messy 12-runner chase. He has already won at Downpatrick over 18f on Good (05-08), with useful course-and-distance form (1-2) and a prior win at the track on good-to-yielding; that is the clearest trip/ground/course fit in the field. He carries a workable 11-5, is only 15 days off the track, and the Galway unseat reads as a one-off on a stiff 18f track rather than a chronic jumping pattern — his form line still shows completion in four of his last five starts, including that Downpatrick success. **Kalsman** earns respect as top weight off OR 100 and a 0.5L Downpatrick near-miss over longer, but Kilbeggan was poor last time and 11-12 is a stiff ask here; market favourite **Whispering Willow** is 0-4 on Good and Keith Donoghue’s recent profile on softening ground is a negative on today’s firmer surface.

The biggest risk to Sea Of Doubt is jumping reliability: the Galway unseat is fresh, and in a competitive handicap any fence error leaves little recovery room against **Pralognan**, who is strongly supported (8.6→4.9) off a Downpatrick CD win and a hot A. Accademia remains the most coherent winner profile on the revised evidence. She maps cleanly onto today’s conditions: a fresh 23-day return off a course win here on 17 July (C 1-1), a useful 5‑1‑1‑5 pattern before that, and an 8lb ratings pull from the three 86‑rated anchors while the market has already compressed her to 1.1. That price is not proof of ability, but the form stack — local course success, light weight in a 0‑85, and Ed Walker/Kieran Shoemark — supports the model’s default rather than forcing an override.

The main risk is that this is not a one‑horse race on paper. River Card (draw 1, Ascot win, David Egan in respectable form) and Raintown (2‑5 at Newbury, CD 1‑2, won over this 10f track in July) both bring course‑and‑trip logic the favourite lacks on Good (G 0‑1), and Mohaaraj/Parlando/Tambora are high‑mark types if fully fit. The saved‑for‑bigger soft pattern and a thin Good‑ground sample also cap how far above the field Accademia can be rated — I agree with the model’s #1, but not at a probability the 1.1 quote implies.

Ebony Maw is the most convincing local angle in an otherwise messy Class 5: he has already won at Ayr over today’s 13f on Good ground (07-06), with useful course-and-distance figures (CD 2-5, C 3-8) and a positive draw in the low third (dr2) where the mild Ayr 13f bias still helps more than dr10–11 types. Jason Hart’s solid six-month numbers add a small connection edge, and at OR 52 he is not exposed on the same mark band as the recent Chester/Musselburgh winners who arrive with sharper profiles and higher weights. I am not treating the blanket @1.1 quotes as evidence—this is a form-and-suitability call, not a market stamp.

The main risk is that this is still a deep 11-runner handicap with several plausible improvers: Cascade Hall brings a fast-return Chester win (LR7) and the best recent ceiling in the field, while Jim Goldie’s triple entry and the “saved-for-bigger” soft pattern on Cascade Hall, Furhaan and Alpine Sierra muddy whether the yard is fully targeting this £5,310 pot. If Cascade Hall repeats his Chester effort, Ebony Maw’s lower OR and prior win under a lenient mark may not be enough.

CursorTwitch · 15%
Risk Sanditon won over C+D here in June and may bounce back from one bad run.
pace map and whether Twitch needs a lead or can stalkSanditon fitness post-Musselburgh 9L defeatEnjoy The Night stable confidence behind the 8.0→5.4 steam
Twitch looks the most coherent win candidate in a messy Class 6. Draw 3 sits in the low third where Wolverhampton 7f winners land about 30% of the time — useful rather than decisive in a 12-runner field — and he maps cleanly to the job: second over 7f on Lingfield AW in April (0.3L), another solid AW run in June, and a 2–18 distance record that fits this trip better than most rivals. At OR 47 he is not burdened out of it, and the 4.9 quote is a fair market lead without the “short banker” profile that burned the board yesterday; this is form-and-draw reasoning, not steam-chasing.

The main danger is Sanditon, who won this exact course and distance in June and is only a tick behind Twitch in the market despite a 9L Musselburgh flop last time — if that was a one-off, his CD 1–5 and Charlie Johnston/Jack Mitchell pairing make him the obvious upset. Enjoy The Night’s 8.0→5.4 move is the other red flag: the bare form (635-79) does not justify it, but heavy support can still mean a ready filly the paper hides.

early pace and whether Interstate sits handy or needs to come off the paceGood vs good-to-firm split for Interstate given 0-0 on Good turfHannon stable intentions between Law Court (Moore) and Lucky Luna in a 9-runner field
Interstate is the logical default: he arrives off a Newcastle AW win (LR15), before which he was a pair of tight 0.3L seconds over 10f on good-to-firm at Sandown and Doncaster — trip and surface progression fit this 10f Good handicap, and the Gosden/Buick pairing is the strongest yard/jockey combo on the card (Buick’s recent Cerro Blanco success supports trusting the setup). Draw 4 sits in the slightly favoured middle third at Newbury ~10f, he carries a workable 9-7 off OR83 in a tightly handicapped field, and the 1-2-2-2 profile reads as a horse still on the upgrade rather than one exposed by the mark. I agree with the model’s #1 despite 0-0 on Good turf, because those two 10f near-misses on GF are the more relevant turf evidence than the surface blank alone.

The biggest risk is Empirical from draw 1: he won over 10f on GF at Ayr last month (D 1-1), maps to the low-third draw bias here, and has prior Newbury experience where stewards felt a right-hand hang cost him no more than half a length — a ready-made “bounce-back” narrative at around 4.0 that is less dependent on translating AW form to turf. Law Court (Moore) is the other live danger on class and connections, but 8f-heavy…

CursorDepalma · 40%
Risk 21.5f on Good may expose stamina limits after recent sub-20f placings and a 0-4 Good record.
proven form beyond 19fNewton Abbot course-specific staying profileearly pace/scenario over 21.5f
Depalma remains the logical pick on balance. Dan Skelton and Harry Skelton are the strongest NH connections on the card, his OR 102 sits near the top of the field, and the career 2-3-2-1 profile shows consistent hurdling without recent P/F/U marks — important over 21.5f. Penzance brings a higher OR (105) and a sharp Worcester second (0.8L, same Good ground and Class 4), but his 0-8 on Good is a sharper going negative than Depalma’s 0-4, and the Hanlon team is far weaker on six‑month yard/jockey ranks. Devon Red is a Worcester fourth on one run; the rest are ruled out by PU/long absences (Dontcontradictme, Ocean Rose, Pappano) or lack of evidence (Black Dakota).

The main worry is trip and ground, not the price. Depalma’s last three runs (4th/6th/8th over 16–19f) do not prove he stays 21.5f on Good at Newton Abbot, and post‑mortem notes on Skelton rides at ~21f flag exactly that stamina pattern when a horse arrives without a clear staying profile. Penzance is the clear second: fresher UK form and the top OR, but he is untested at this trip and his Good record is worse. I agree with the model default rather than overriding to Penzance on one strong Worcester run.

CursorLittle Miss India · 17%
Risk Melting Snow repeats recent Wolverhampton AW form with the card's top jockey.
pace/map from low draws (Lilly Lux dr1, Pipily dr2)Melting Snow's exact winning trip/distance here on 09-01Pipily's AW debut suitability at 9.5f
Little Miss India is the most coherent profile for a Wolverhampton 9.5f Class 5 on standard AW: joint-top on OR 70, proven course-and-distance (1-2 CD, including a March win over 10f here), and solid going/distance records (3-9 G, 1-7 D). Draw 8 sits in the historically stronger high third at this trip (~38% of winners), which helps in an eight-runner field where low stalls are underrepresented. The Doncaster fifth (1.5L, LR7) reads as a respectable prep rather than a negative, and the drift to 10.0 improves the price versus the model’s edge without undermining the form case—unlike the market steamers.

The biggest risk is Melting Snow: a 17-day AW winner at this track (C 1-1) with Billy Loughnane in strong 6-month form and a useful mark at OR 64. Pipily at 1.1 is the obvious trap—four runs, no AW/going form, and yesterday’s post-mortem flagged sub-2.2 bankers losing; short price is not ability proof here. Lilly Lux’s steam and top weight are offset by 130 days off and a low draw in a race that mildly favors high stalls.
NVIDIALittle Miss India · 38%
Risk Draw 8 at a 9.5f track where high draws have slightly lower strike rates; she may need early momentum to secure a clear run.
OR consistency under weightWhether she can get cover without over-racing from a wide draw
Analysis: Little Miss India has the class edge and proven AW 10f form, winning here last prep at 3.8; she handles this standard better than Lilly Lux who steps up in trip and comes from a lower rating, while Melting Snow and Speculative lack the consistency. The draw 8 is unlucky but her course-distance mastery and 70 OR suggest she can overcome it, especially if she settles positively from the mid-range draw.

Soft ground and trip suited a filly with enough experience to handle a nine-runner handicap despite limited Ayr form (D 0-1).
Right The board pick Diplomata was the right side of the race: firming price, defensible OR, and elite trainer rank matched the winner.

Glorious Kitty is the most coherent 8f profile in a messy Class 5: OR 70 keeps her in the weights, she is 1-3 at Ayr with CD 1-1, and her latest Ripon 8f on Good (6/9, 0.3L) maps cleanly onto today’s trip and ground. Draw 3 sits in the weaker low third at Ayr (~24% over six years), but that is a modest headwind rather than a disqualifier in an 11-runner field where no runner dominates on form. Invincible Ruby’s York second (2/18, 0.5L) shows a higher ceiling, yet 0-1 at 8f, 0-2 on Good, and a disappointing Haydock rebound argue she needs everything to fall right; Motawaared (high draw, LR6, close Ayr 10f) and Jewel Maker (recent win, 2-18 at trip) are each-way claims rather than win-led.

The biggest risk to Kitty is ground: she is 0-4 on Good-to-Soft today versus useful runs on Good/Soft elsewhere — if the surface rides genuinely soft rather than good-to-soft, her win chance drops materially. Flying Fletcher tops the weights on OR 72 but reads like a possible pacemaker with patchy recent form and a saved-for-bigger pattern; Empirestateofmind’s CD 1-1 is tempting on paper but 040990 form and 0-4 on Good are hard to ignore.

This is a deep, competitive Class 1 with no clear standout from the Going baseline, so the call rests on course-and-distance proof, ground suitability, and whether recent freshness outweighs class. **Beautiful Diamond** is the pick: top OR (105), the only runner with meaningful market support (@ 3.0), proven on today’s going (G 1-2), and a standout Ayr record (C 3-4, CD 3-4) with three straight Class 1 placings — including 3rd here over 5f beaten only 0.1L. Draw 4 sits in the low third on a 15-runner sprint where the rail often matters on good to soft. Burke’s **Lam Yai** (fresh Doncaster C1 winner, 2nd at Ayr, low draw) and **Fluorescence** (dr2, Pontefract winner, Tudhope/Bethell) are the main dangers, but neither combines Diamond’s rating, ground wins, and course depth.

The biggest risk is the **90-day layoff** — sprint fitness after such a gap is unverified, and in a 15-runner heat one slow break or stiff finish leaves little recovery room. **Novamay** (CD 2-2 at Ayr) is a soft each-way angle from a high draw but looks outclassed on OR stepping from a C4 win to this level.

This is a messy 13-runner 0–100 handicap where nothing looks truly bankable, but **Mercurial Sea** has the clearest profile on trip, ground and track: he was only 5L behind the winner in second over this exact 18f on good at Downpatrick in May, then closed to a neck off the winner over 22f here on good-to-yielding — so he already handles the track and a stiff 2¼m+. The 8282-6 line is consistent rather than flashy, and the 6.0→4.7 move is supportive without being a sub-2.2 trap after yesterday’s board lesson on short public horses. **John Dixen** shares favouritism on light weight and a Rothwell blinkers change, but `306-00` and a 12L defeat over 22f at Ballinrobe are hard to ignore when **Lucky This Time** is in the same yard at 75.0; I prefer the proven course-placed profile over the speculative improver.

The biggest risk is that Mercurial Sea still reads like a perennial placed horse (12 runs, no obvious winning habit) in a field where **Pahlavi** is a literal course-and-distance winner from the 2025 18f good handicap here (analog SP 8.5) and **Tropical Twist** brings the highest mark off a good-ground Wexford win — even if 12st and a summer PU cap enthusiasm.
